paragraphs.text: Leslie Nielsen’s childhood was a difficult one, but he had one particular shining star in his life—his uncle, who was a well-known actor. The admiration and respect his uncle earned inspired Nielsen to make a career (职业) in acting. Even though he often felt he would be discovered to be a no-talent, he moved forward, gaining a scholarship to the Neighborhood Playhouse and making his first television appearance a few years later in 1948. However, becoming a full-time, successful actor would still be an uphill battle for another eight years until he landed a number of film roles that finally got him noticed.

But even then, what he had wasn’t quite what he wanted. Nielsen always felt he should be doing comedy but his good looks and distinguished voice kept him busy in dramatic roles. It wasn’t until 1980—32 years into his career—that he landed the role it would seem he was made for in Airplane! That movie led him into the second half of his career where his comedic presence alone could make a movie a financial success even when movie reviewers would not rate it highly.

Did Nielsen then feel content in his career? Yes and no. He was thrilled to be doing the comedy that he always felt he should do, but even during his last few years, he always had a sense of curiosity, wondering what new role or challenge might be just around the corner. He never stopped working, never retired.

Leslie Nielsen’s devotion to acting is wonderfully inspiring. He built a hugely successful career with little more than plain old hard work and determination. He showed us that even a single desire, never given up on, can make for a remarkable life.

We live in a town with three beaches. There are two parks less than 10 minutes’ walk from home where neighbourhood children gather to play. However, what my children want to do after school is pick up a screen—any screen—and stare at it for hours. They are not alone. Today’s children spend an average of four and a half hours a day looking at screens, split between watching television and using the Internet.

In the past few years, an increasing number of people and organisations have begun coming up with plans to counter this trend. A couple of years ago, film-maker David Bond realised that his children, then aged five and three, were attached to screens to the point where he was able to say “chocolate” into his three-year-old son’s ear without getting a response. He realised that something needed to change, and, being a London media type, appointed himself “marketing director for Nature”. He documented his journey as he set about treating nature as a brand to be marketed to young people. The result was Project Wild Thing, a film which charts the birth of the Wild Network, a group of organisations with the common goal of getting children out into nature.

“Just five more minutes outdoors can make a difference,” David Bond says. “There is a lot of really interesting evidence which seems to be suggesting that if children are inspired up to the age of seven, then being outdoors will be a habit for life.” His own children have got into the habit of playing outside now: “We just send them out into the garden and tell them not to come back in for a while.”
Summer is upon us. There is an amazing world out there, and it needs our children as much as they need it. Let us get them out and let them play.

If you ever get the impression that your dog can “tell” whether you look content or annoyed, you may be onto something. Dogs may indeed be able to distinguish between happy and angry human faces, according to a new study.

Researchers trained a group of 11 dogs to distinguish between images (图像) of the same person making either a happy or an angry face. During the training stage, each dog was shown only the upper half or the lower half of the person’s face. The researchers then tested the dogs’ ability to distinguish between human facial expressions by showing them the other half of the person’s face or images totally different from the ones used in training. The researchers found that the dogs were able to pick the angry or happy face by touching a picture of it with their noses more often than one would expect by random chance.

The study showed the animals had figured out how to apply what they learned about human faces during training to new faces in the testing stage. “We can rule out that the dogs simply distinguish between the pictures based on a simple cue, such as the sight of teeth,” said study author Corsin Muller. “Instead, our results suggest that the successful dogs realized that a smiling mouth means the same thing as smiling eyes, and the same rule applies to an angry mouth having the same meaning as angry eyes.”
“With our study, we think we can now confidently conclude that at least some dogs can distinguish human facial expressions,” Muller told Live Science.

At this point, it is not clear why dogs seem to be equipped with the ability to recognize different facial expressions in humans. “To us, the most likely explanation appears to be that the basis lies in their living with humans, which gives them a lot of exposure to human facial expressions,” and this exposure has provided them with many chances to learn to distinguish between them, Muller said.

paragraphs.text: You’ve got mail…and it’s a postcard

Paulo Magalhaes, a 34-year-old Portuguese computer engineer, loves to open his mailbox and find a brightly colored picture of Rome’s Colosseum. Or Africa’s Victoria Falls. Or China’s Great Wall. __31__ 1

“I often send postcards to family and friends,” he says to China Daily, “but you can imagine that after a while, you never receive as many as you send, and you realize that not everyone is into it. __32__ 2  “ Seeking other like-minded souls, however, Paulo started looking in a somewhat unlikely place: online. Many would say the Internet is a place for people who have given up on the traditional postal service, but Paulo’s hunch (直觉) paid off.

Today his hobby has developed into the website postcrossing. com, a social network that has grown to 575,217 registered users in 214 countries and regions since he started it 10 years ago. __33__ 3   Running the website has almost turned into a full-time job.

Language is certainly a barrier for many people. For postcrossing to work worldwide, a common communication language is needed so that everyone can understand each other. As cool as it may be to receive a postcard written in Chinese, the concept doesn’t work if one doesn’t understand it. __34__ 4   So a common language is required and in postcrossing that’s English since it’s widely spoken.

“Many people in China have limited exposure to English. __35__ 5   That said, we know of many postcrossing members, including Chinese, who have actually improved their English skills through their use of postcrossing,” Paulo says.

It doesn’t impress like George Washington’s plantation on the Potomac, but Lincoln’s home in downtown Springfield, Illinois, __56__ (prove) irresistible to visitors since it opened to the public. Beautifully restored (修复) to its 1860 appearance, the house was Abraham and Mary Lincoln’s home for 17 years. In 1844 they bought it __57__1,200 and some land from Charles Dresser, who performed their __58__ (marry) ceremony in 1842.

When the house was built, it was much __59__ (small) than it is today. Mary’s niece wrote, “The little home __60__ (paint) white. It was sweet and fresh. Mary loved it. She was extremely pretty, and her house was a reflection of __61__ (she) , everything in good taste and in perfect order.”

Although Mary loved flowers, __62__she nor her husband was known as a gardener. A long-time neighbor said they never planted trees and only kept a garden for one year. Mary’s sister, Frances Todd Wallace, often came over __63__ (plant) flowers in the front yard.

昨天你参观了学校举办的学生国画作品展。请给校英文报写一篇宣传稿，内容包括：
（1）展览时间
（2）观展感受；
（3）推荐观展。
（1）词数80左右；
（2）可以适当增加细节，以使行文连贯。

My dad, George, only had an eighth grade education. A quiet man, he didn’t understand my world of school activities. From age 14, he worked. And his dad, Albert, took the money my dad earned and used it to pay family expenses.

I didn’t really understand his world either: He was a livestock trucker, and I thought that I would surpass (超过) anything he had accomplished by the time I walked across the stage at high school graduation.

Summers in the mid-70s were spent at home shooting baskets, hitting a baseball, or throwing a football, preparing for my future as a quarterback on a football team. In poor weather, I read about sports or practiced my trombone (长号) .

The summer before my eighth grade I was one of a group of boys that a neighboring farmer hired to work in his field. He explained our basic task, the tractor fired up and we were off, riding down the field looking for weeds to spray with chemicals. After a short way, the farmer stopped and pointed at a weed which we missed. Then we began again. This happened over and over, but we soon learned to identify different grasses like cockleburs, lamb’s-quarters, foxtails, and the king of weeds, the pretty purple thistle. It was tiring work, but I looked forward to the pay, even though I wasn’t sure how much it would amount to.
At home, my dad said, “A job’s a big step to growing up. I’m glad you will be contributing to the household.” My dad’s words made me realize that my earnings might not be mine to do with as I wished.
My labors lasted about two weeks, and the farmer said there might be more work, but I wasn’t interested. I decided it was not fair that I had to contribute my money.

group-zj-2021-jun-reading-a.overview: 本文是一篇人物传记，记述著名演员 Leslie Nielsen 的演艺生涯。文章按时间顺序展开：从他童年受当演员的叔叔启发立志从艺，到历经多年奋斗终于在喜剧中找到归属，再到他一生从不退休、始终保持好奇心，最后点明他凭借坚持与努力成就了非凡人生。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文按时间线推进：起因（受叔叔启发立志）→ 奋斗（长期演正剧却渴望喜剧，1980年凭《Airplane!》转型）→ 心态（满足又始终好奇，从不退休）→ 主旨升华（坚持单一梦想成就非凡人生）。

paragraphs.summary: Nielsen 童年艰难，但当知名演员的叔叔成为他的指路明星，叔叔赢得的钦佩与尊重激发他立志从艺；尽管常怕自己没天赋，他仍不断前进，获奖学金、1948年首登荧屏，又经八年苦战才靠若干电影角色崭露头角。
paragraphs.function: 开篇交代人物从艺的起因（受叔叔启发）与早期奋斗历程，回答第21题。

paragraphs.summary: 即便出名后，所得仍非所愿：他一直觉得自己该演喜剧，但好相貌和独特嗓音让他困于正剧角色；直到1980年（入行32年）凭《Airplane!》找到天造之合的角色，由此进入生涯下半场——其喜剧魅力即便影评不高也能让电影盈利。
paragraphs.function: 转折段，叙述其职业生涯下半场的转型与喜剧上的商业成功，回答第22题。

paragraphs.summary: 回答他是否满足：既满足又不满足——能演一直想演的喜剧令他激动，但即便晚年仍保持好奇，想着下一个新角色或挑战；他从不停止工作，从不退休。
paragraphs.function: 刻画其晚年心态，承上启下，体现其对事业的持续热情。

paragraphs.summary: 总结升华：Nielsen 对表演的投入极具激励性，他几乎仅凭质朴的努力与决心建立辉煌事业，向我们证明：只要不放弃，单一的愿望也能成就非凡人生。
paragraphs.function: 结尾点题升华，揭示文章主旨（坚持梦想），回答第23题。

group-zj-2021-jun-reading-b.overview: 本文是一篇议论性说明文，针对当下儿童沉迷电子屏幕的问题，介绍了电影人David Bond如何把“自然”当作品牌推销给孩子（Project Wild Thing 与 Wild Network），呼吁让孩子走出户外、回归自然。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文按“提出问题—介绍应对—引用观点—发出呼吁”的逻辑展开：先以作者自家孩子沉迷屏幕引出普遍现象，再介绍David Bond把自然当品牌营销的做法，接着引用其观点强调早期户外习惯的重要性，最后号召让孩子出门玩耍。

paragraphs.summary: 作者家附近虽有海滩和公园，但自家孩子放学后只想盯着屏幕，并指出这是当今儿童的普遍现象。
paragraphs.function: 提出问题：以个人经历切入，引出儿童长时间看屏幕的普遍现象。

paragraphs.summary: 介绍电影人David Bond因孩子沉迷屏幕而行动，自封“自然的营销总监”，把自然当品牌推销，并拍摄纪录片Project Wild Thing，催生了致力于让孩子走进自然的Wild Network。
paragraphs.function: 介绍应对措施：呈现一个具体人物如何用营销手段应对该问题。

paragraphs.summary: 引用David Bond的话，指出哪怕多五分钟户外时间也有意义，七岁前受到熏陶可形成终身户外习惯，并以自己孩子已养成户外玩耍习惯为例。
paragraphs.function: 引证观点：用专家话语与亲身实例支撑户外活动的价值。

paragraphs.summary: 夏天来临，户外世界精彩且需要孩子，作者呼吁让孩子走出去尽情玩耍。
paragraphs.function: 总结呼吁：以号召收尾，升华主题。

group-zj-2021-jun-reading-c.overview: 本文是一篇科普说明文，介绍了一项关于狗能否分辨人类面部表情的新研究。研究发现，至少部分狗能够区分人类高兴和生气的面孔，并探讨了产生这一能力的可能原因。

discourseStructure.summary: 文章按照"提出结论—介绍实验—解读结果—得出结论—探讨原因"的顺序展开：先抛出狗能分辨人类表情的研究结论，再描述训练与测试的实验过程，接着借研究者之口解读结果含义，重申结论，最后分析狗具备此能力的可能成因。

paragraphs.summary: 引出话题：如果你觉得狗能看出你高兴还是恼火，可能确有其事；一项新研究表明狗或许能区分人类高兴与生气的面孔。
paragraphs.function: 以读者的日常体验切入，引出研究的核心发现，点明文章主题。

paragraphs.summary: 介绍实验过程：研究者训练11只狗区分同一人高兴或生气的面孔图像，训练时只展示半张脸，测试时用另一半脸或全新图像，结果狗辨认表情的成功率高于随机概率。
paragraphs.function: 详细描述研究的训练与测试方法及结果，提供支撑结论的实验证据。

paragraphs.summary: 解读结果：狗把训练中学到的关于人脸的知识迁移到新面孔；研究者指出可排除狗仅凭露齿等简单线索辨别，成功的狗领悟到笑的嘴和笑的眼睛含义相同。
paragraphs.function: 借研究作者之口阐释实验结果的深层含义，排除简单线索的解释。

paragraphs.summary: 得出结论：研究者表示现在可以有把握地断定，至少一些狗能够区分人类的面部表情。
paragraphs.function: 概括并重申研究的核心结论。

paragraphs.summary: 探讨原因：目前尚不清楚狗为何具备识别人类表情的能力，研究者认为最可能的解释是狗与人类共同生活，大量接触人类面部表情，从而获得学习区分的机会。
paragraphs.function: 分析研究发现背后的可能成因，对全文进行延伸性收尾。

trap.sourceEntity: the person’s face（被拍摄/展示的是人的脸）
trap.optionText: The dogs were photographed before the test.
trap.optionEntity: The dogs were photographed（被拍摄的是狗）
trap.explanation: 原文中被展示在图像里的是"人"的脸，狗是观看者；选项把被拍摄对象错配成"狗"，与原文不符。

locationParaphrases.sourceText: Pictures used in the two stages were different
locationParaphrases.targetText: images totally different from the ones used in training
locationParaphrases.note: 正确选项 Pictures used in the two stages were different 对应原文 images totally different from the ones used in training，将"测试图片与训练图片完全不同"概括为"两阶段图片不同"。

q-zj-2021-jun-030.questionFocus: 考查对末段主旨的概括，即最后一段主要讲了什么内容。
q-zj-2021-jun-030.stemTranslationZh: 最后一段主要讲的是什么？

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 对未来研究的一条建议。

trap.claim: 最后一段是对未来研究提出建议
trap.explanation: 原文未提及对今后研究的任何建议。末段讨论的是狗具备识别表情能力的可能原因，而非提出后续研究方向。

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 对研究发现的一个可能原因。

evidence.quote: the most likely explanation appears to be that the basis lies in their living with humans, which gives them a lot of exposure to human facial expressions
evidence.anchor: 最可能的解释：与人共同生活、大量接触人脸

evidence.quote: it is not clear why dogs seem to be equipped with the ability to recognize different facial expressions in humans
evidence.anchor: 尚不清楚狗为何具备识别表情的能力（引出原因探讨）

trap.sourceText: it is not clear why dogs seem to be equipped with the ability to recognize different facial expressions in humans
trap.optionText: A major limitation of the study.
trap.relationNote: 末段 it is not clear why（尚不清楚原因）易被误读为研究存在"局限"。但该句是为引出对成因的推测，整段重心在给出"可能原因"，并非陈述研究的不足之处。

trapEvidence.quote: it is not clear why dogs seem to be equipped with the ability to recognize different facial expressions in humans
trapEvidence.anchor: 尚不清楚原因（引出推测，非陈述局限）

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 对研究方法的一个说明。

trap.sourceQuote: this exposure has provided them with many chances to learn to distinguish between them
trap.sourceHighlight: many chances to learn to distinguish
trap.optionText: An explanation of the research method.
trap.explanation: 对研究方法（训练与测试过程）的说明出现在第二段，而非末段。末段说明的是狗习得该能力的"原因"，选项把末段内容偷换成"研究方法"，张冠李戴。

locationParaphrases.sourceText: A possible reason for the study findings
locationParaphrases.targetText: the most likely explanation appears to be that the basis lies in their living with humans
locationParaphrases.note: 正确选项 A possible reason（一个可能原因）对应末段 the most likely explanation（最可能的解释），possible reason 与 likely explanation 为同义替换。
